newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovakia must be more active on FDI - diplomat.
newsitem.headline: Slovakia must be more active on FDI - diplomat.

text.p: Slovakia should do more to attract foreign investment, despite recent successes, British ambassador Peter Harborne said on Wednesday.

"All the conditions exist here and there have already been several successful investment projects, but the (Slovak) government would need to be even more pro-active," he said at the Slovak launch of a new British trade drive in central Europe.
Foreign direct investment in Slovakia has lagged behind some other countries in the region and analysts have blamed political uncertainty and an indifferent government.
Called "Open for Business Central Europe" the campaign aims to double British exports to the region.

"Our goal is to double our overall exports from the present two billion to four billion sterling to the countries of the region -- Slovakia, the Czech Republic, Poland, Hungary and Slovenia," Harborne said announcing the start of the campaign.

Britain's exports to Slovakia grew from 10.6 million pounds in 1993 to 70.3 million pounds for the first nine months of last year, while imports grew from 13 million pounds to 120.4 million pounds over the same period, according to official figures.
The largest British investors in Slovakia are retailer Tesco Plc, sugar refiner Tate and Lyle and Royal Dutch/Shell with its petrol stations.

Britain's trade volume with the five countries in the 1990-95 period totalled 19 billion sterling with exports growing by 35 percent overall in 1995, Britain's fastest export growth rate in any region in the world, Harborne said.
The ambassador said the aim of the campaign was to encourage small and medium-sized British business to explore trade openings in central Europe.
"The main objective is to inform on the scope of the market and its potential," Harborne said, adding that Britain still lagged behind Germany and Austria as the largest trade partner in the region.
